title: LocalVector crash on non-trivial copy/move/dtor types when reserve/resize need a new memory block
body:
### Tested versions

4.4.1-stable

### System information

Web (emscripten)

### Issue description

Hi Godot friends 🍅 🧚 🐱 🤖

I think ```LocalVector``` assumes it can do a bitwise-copy of the data when doing a memrealloc (e.g. on resize/reserve). If realloc manages to extend the current memory block, then I think it's fine. But if realloc needs to use a completely new memory block, then it will bitwise-copy current data, which is not correct if the type is not trivially copyable. So we would probably need to use placement new with copy/move ctor on non-trivially copyable/movable types.

And same for non-trivially destructible types. It just frees the memory block without destructing the objects in the old block.

I have not experienced the crash in desktop, but it is a 100% crash in web (emscripten + wasm).
If I replace my ```LocalVector``` with ```std::vector```, it does not crash anymore.
I have a heavily modified engine, so I can't give you repro steps for the crash as it happens in a very custom scenario.

@Ivorforce, as I've seen you are doing related changes, hope this helps! 😄  
Thanks a lot! 🥰

### Steps to reproduce

Can't give repro steps for crash. But you can see it's not doing the right thing if you compare ```LocalVector``` behavior vs ```std::vector``` behavior on a struct such as:

```
struct Bar { int a; Bar() { } ~Bar() { print_line("Dtor"); } Bar(const Bar&) { print_line("Copy Ctor"); } };
```

Do this:
```
LocalVector<Bar> vector;
vector.resize(10);
vector.resize(100); // <<<<< PUT BREAKPOINT HERE;
```
Do the same but using ```std::vector``` instead of ```LocalVector```.
Observe how ```std::vector``` calls copy-ctors and dtors for the 10 first elements, but ```LocalVector``` does not.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Write the example anywhere in c++ engine code
